title: NHS: Missed or late periods
keywords: late period missed periods menstrual cycle irregular causes stress weight exercise contraception pregnancy
content: A late or missed period can happen for many reasons, including pregnancy, stress, sudden weight loss, being overweight, too much exercise, or some forms of contraception. If pregnancy is possible, a pregnancy test can help clarify the cause. Contact a healthcare professional if you are concerned, miss periods repeatedly, or have other symptoms.

title: NHS: Doing a pregnancy test
keywords: pregnancy test pregnant late missed period when test
content: Most pregnancy tests are most reliable from the first day of a missed period. If you do not know when your next period is due, test at least 21 days after unprotected sex. Follow the instructions that come with the test.

title: NHS: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
keywords: pcos polycystic ovary syndrome irregular periods acne hair fertility diagnosis
content: PCOS is one possible cause of irregular periods, but irregular periods can have many causes. A healthcare professional assesses symptoms and may arrange tests; a late period alone cannot establish that someone has PCOS.

title: NHS: Period problems
keywords: period pain heavy bleeding period problems doctor healthcare professional severe bleeding urgent
content: Period problems can have different causes. Seek medical advice if period pain or bleeding is severe, affects daily life, or is a change from what is usual for you. Sudden severe pain or very heavy bleeding may need urgent assessment.

title: NHS: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS)
keywords: pms premenstrual syndrome symptoms before period mood changes irritability bloating breast tenderness headaches tiredness
content: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) can cause symptoms in the days or weeks before a period. Symptoms can include mood changes, irritability, feeling upset or anxious, tiredness, difficulty sleeping, bloating, breast tenderness, headaches and changes in appetite. Symptoms can vary between people and may change over time.

title: NHS: Period pain
keywords: period pain cramps menstrual pain abdominal pain painful periods dysmenorrhoea
content: Period pain is common and usually happens around the start of a period. It can feel like painful cramps in the lower abdomen and may last for several days. See a healthcare professional if the pain is severe, getting worse, or affecting daily activities.

title: NHS: Mental health and wellbeing
keywords: mental health stress anxiety depression mood wellbeing sleep emotional health
content: Mental health can affect how a person thinks, feels and behaves. Looking after mental wellbeing can include getting enough sleep, staying physically active, maintaining connections with other people and seeking support when difficulties are affecting everyday life.

title: NHS: Women's health
keywords: womens health periods reproductive health contraception pregnancy menstrual health health
content: Women's health includes areas such as menstrual health, reproductive health, pregnancy and contraception. Symptoms that are persistent, severe, unusual for you or affecting daily life may need assessment from a healthcare professional.

title: NHS: Methods of contraception
keywords: contraception birth control pregnancy prevention condom pill implant coil IUD IUS hormonal emergency
content: There are several types of contraception, including condoms, hormonal methods, intrauterine devices and systems, and emergency contraception. Methods differ in how they are used and how well they prevent pregnancy. Condoms also help reduce the risk of sexually transmitted infections; other contraception methods do not protect against STIs. A healthcare professional can help discuss suitable options.

title: NHS: Endometriosis
keywords: endometriosis womb lining tissue period pain pelvic pain heavy bleeding sex fertility symptoms
content: Endometriosis is a condition where tissue similar to the lining of the womb grows in other places, such as the ovaries or fallopian tubes. Symptoms can include severe period pain, pelvic pain, heavy periods, pain during or after sex, and difficulty getting pregnant, but they vary and some people have no symptoms. If symptoms affect daily life or you are concerned, speak to a healthcare professional; symptoms alone cannot confirm a diagnosis.

title: NHS: Menopause and perimenopause symptoms
keywords: menopause perimenopause hot flushes night sweats periods sleep mood anxiety symptoms
content: Menopause and perimenopause symptoms vary. They can include changes to periods, hot flushes, night sweats, difficulty sleeping, and changes in mood. Symptoms may affect daily life, and a GP can discuss support and treatment options.

title: NHS: Infertility
keywords: fertility infertility conceive conception trying pregnant pregnancy difficulty seek help year age
content: Fertility difficulties can affect either partner, so assessment may involve both. If you have not conceived after a year of trying, speak to a GP; seek advice sooner if you are 36 or over or have a known reason to be concerned about fertility. A healthcare professional can discuss possible causes and appropriate tests.

title: NHS: STI testing and treatment
keywords: sexual health sexually transmitted infection STI test testing treatment clinic screening chlamydia gonorrhoea
content: NHS sexual health services can provide information, STI testing and treatment. Some infections do not cause noticeable symptoms, so testing may be appropriate after possible exposure or if you are concerned. Services and testing options vary by area; use the NHS service finder or contact a local sexual health service for advice.

title: PMDD
keywords: PMDD, premenstrual dysphoric disorder, PMS, premenstrual syndrome, ovulation, hormone levels, serotonin, irritability, depression, anxiety, panic attacks, mood swings, bloating, breast tenderness, cramps, fatigue, sertraline, fluoxetine, paroxetine, SSRIs, antidepressants, birth control pills, meditation, yoga, lifestyle changes
content: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) is a severe form of premenstrual syndrome (PMS) that can cause significant mood changes and physical symptoms in the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle. Symptoms may include irritability, depression, anxiety, panic attacks, mood swings, bloating, breast tenderness, cramps, and fatigue. Treatment options can include lifestyle changes, medication such as SSRIs, and birth control pills.

title: NHS: Heavy Periods
keywords: heavy periods menorrhagia menstrual bleeding excessive bleeding periods
content: Heavy periods, also known as menorrhagia, involve excessive menstrual bleeding that can interfere with daily life. Symptoms may include soaking through one or more sanitary pads or tampons every hour for several consecutive hours, needing to use double protection, or passing large blood clots. It's important to see a healthcare professional for assessment and management options.

title: Wellbeing of Women: Severe Period Pain
keywords: severe period pain dysmenorrhoea menstrual cramps abdominal pain
content: Severe period pain, also known as dysmenorrhoea, involves intense menstrual cramps that can interfere with daily activities. It is important to seek medical advice if the pain is severe, persistent, or unusual for you.

title: WellBeingOfWomen: Fibroids
keywords: fibroids uterine fibroids leiomyomas benign tumors menstrual bleeding pelvic pain
content: Fibroids, also known as uterine fibroids or leiomyomas, are non-cancerous growths in the uterus that can cause symptoms such as heavy menstrual bleeding, pelvic pain, and pressure on the bladder or bowel. Treatment options vary depending on the size, location, and severity of symptoms and may include medication or surgical interventions.

title: Wellbeing of Women: Adenomyosis
keywords: adenomyosis endometrial tissue uterine wall heavy menstrual bleeding pelvic pain
content: Adenomyosis is a condition where the endometrial tissue grows into the muscular wall of the uterus, causing heavy menstrual bleeding and pelvic pain. Treatment options may include medication or surgical interventions depending on the severity of symptoms.

title: Wellbeing of Women: Endometriosis
keywords: endometriosis endometrial tissue pelvic pain heavy menstrual bleeding infertility
content: Endometriosis is a condition where the tissue similar to the lining of the uterus grows outside the uterus, causing pelvic pain, heavy menstrual bleeding, and sometimes infertility. Treatment options may include medication or surgical interventions depending on the severity of symptoms.

title: NHS: Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS)
keywords: polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome PMOS hormonal imbalance menstrual irregularities infertility
content: Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS) is a rare hormonal disorder that affects the ovaries and other endocrine glands, leading to symptoms such as menstrual irregularities, infertility, and metabolic issues. Management may include lifestyle changes, medication, and regular monitoring by healthcare professionals.

title: Canberra Health Services: Period Impact and Pain Assessment (PIPPA)
keywords: period impact pain assessment PIPPA endometriosis menstrual pain
content: The Period Impact and Pain Assessment (PIPPA) is a service provided by the Canberra Endometriosis Centre to evaluate the impact of menstrual pain on daily life and to guide appropriate management and treatment options.

title: NHS Wales: Painful periods and pain relief
keywords: contacting healthcare providers painful periods menstrual pain cramps menstrual cycle endometriosis adenomyosis fibroids pelvic inflammatory disease IUD coil heat pad hormonal contraception
content: Period pain is common before or during periods, usually lasting up to 3 days, and can often be eased at home with heat, gentle exercise, massage or painkillers like paracetamol or ibuprofen. It can also stem from conditions such as endometriosis, fibroids or pelvic inflammatory disease, so severe or worsening pain — or pain that disrupts daily life — warrants seeing a GP, who may suggest stronger anti-inflammatories, a TENS machine or hormonal contraception. For painful periods or menstrual pain, contacting healthcare providers is essential for proper diagnosis and management; NHS Wales provides guidance on seeking medical advice and support.

title: When to seek mental health support
keywords: mental health support, seeking help, mental health resources
content: It is important to seek mental health support when experiencing persistent emotional distress, mood changes, or other mental health concerns. The WHO provides guidance on recognizing the need for support and accessing appropriate mental health resources.

title: Infections
keywords: toxic shock syndrome, TSS, Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pyogenes, tampons, bacterial infection, toxins ,Secondary: super-absorbent tampons, menstrual cups, skin wounds, burns, surgery, high fever, low blood pressure, sunburn-like rash, organ dysfunction, antibiotics, prevention, treatment
content: Toxic shock syndrome (TSS) is a rare but life-threatening condition caused by bacterial toxins, most often Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes, leading to fever, rash, low blood pressure, and organ dysfunction. In menstruation, it's linked mainly to tampon use — especially super-absorbent tampons or those left in too long — which create conditions favoring bacterial growth, so changing tampons every 4–6 hours and using the lowest absorbency needed greatly reduces risk.

title: Iron deficiency and sources
keywords: Iron, red blood cells, oxygen, iron deficiency anaemia, menstrual period, heavy periods, 14.8mg, women aged 19–49, iron supplements, iron-rich foods
content: Iron needs rise during the menstrual years: women aged 19–49 need 14.8mg daily — notably higher than the 8.7mg for men or women over 50 — because iron is lost through menstrual blood. Those with heavy periods are especially at risk of iron deficiency anaemia and may need supplements, so iron-rich foods (beans, nuts, dried fruit, fortified cereals, red meat) are particularly important.

title: Reason for periods
keywords: Periods, menstrual cycle, reasons for periods, menstrual health, puberty, pregnancy
content: Periods occur as part of the menstrual cycle, which prepares the body for pregnancy. They are a sign that the reproductive system is functioning normally. Understanding the reasons for periods helps in managing menstrual health and recognizing any abnormalities.

title: Menstrual Cycle Information
keywords: Menstrual cycle, periods, menstrual health, information leaflet
content: This leaflet provides detailed information about the menstrual cycle, including the different phases, what is considered normal, and tips for managing menstrual health.
